edition.locus: Vossius 1684 Opera omnia (archive bub_gb_DY2xvRwPetMC), Latin column, Duodecim Capita de Fide, Cap. III, printed p. 3 (PDF p. 27)

source_text: Si quis dicit hominem perfectum assumptum esse a Christo, tanquam unum ex prophetis; et non confitetur ipsum incarnatione ex Virgine factum hominem, in Bethleem natum, et in Nazaret educatum, et qui progressum in aetate ostendit, et cursum temporum complevit; in Iordane baptizatus est, et a Patre testimonium hoc accepit: Hic est filius meus dilectus, sicut scriptum est; anathema sit. Qua ratione dici potest homo perfectus a Domino assumptus, tanquam unus ex prophetis; cum ipse Dominus per incarnationem ex Virgine homo factus sit? Ideo scriptum est: Primus homo ex terra terrenus. Postquam vero is, qui ex terra formatus erat, in terram abiit; secundus homo factus, in caelos ascendit. Et dicitur primus Adam, et novissimus Adam. Et sicut in confesso est, secundum ex primo esse, quantum ad carnem attinet; unde et homo, et filius hominis Christus: ita quoque testatum est, quod secundus sit Salvator primi, propter quem etiam e caelo descendit. Quoniam autem Verbum e caelo descendens, et homo factum in caelos ascendit; ideo et e caelo secundus Adam esse dicitur.
thought_title: Christ is not a man taken up like one of the prophets
orientation: Gregory condemns the view that Christ took up a complete man as one more prophet, and answers from Paul's contrast of the first Adam from the earth and the second Adam from heaven.
pass_a_gloss: If anyone says [that] a perfect man (homo perfectus) [was] assumed (assumptum) by Christ, as one of the prophets; and does not confess (confitetur) him [to have been] made man by incarnation (incarnatione) from the Virgin, born in Bethlehem, brought up (educatum) in Nazareth, and who showed progress (progressum) in age (aetate), and completed the course of the times (cursum temporum); was baptized in the Jordan, and received from the Father this testimony (testimonium): This is my beloved Son, as it is written; let him be anathema. By what reason can a perfect man be said [to be] assumed by the Lord as one of the prophets, when the Lord himself through incarnation from the Virgin was made man? Therefore it is written: The first man from earth, earthly (terrenus). But after he who had been formed (formatus) from earth went away into earth, having been made the second man, he ascended into the heavens. And there is said [to be] the first Adam and the last (novissimus) Adam. And as it is acknowledged (in confesso est) [that] the second is from the first as far as concerns the flesh (carnem), whence Christ [is] both man and son of man (filius hominis): so too it is testified that the second is Savior (Salvator) of the first, on account of whom he also descended from heaven. Since the Word (Verbum) descending from heaven, and made man, ascended into the heavens; therefore the second Adam is also said to be from heaven.

pass_b_english: If anyone says that a perfect man was taken up by Christ like one of the prophets, and does not confess that he himself became man by incarnation from the Virgin, was born in Bethlehem and brought up in Nazareth, showed growth in age (Luke 2:52) and completed the course of time, was baptized in the Jordan and received from the Father this testimony, “This is my beloved Son” (Matthew 3:17), as it is written, let him be anathema.

For how can it be said that a perfect man was taken up by the Lord like one of the prophets, when the Lord himself became man through incarnation from the Virgin? That is why it is written, “The first man was from the earth, earthly” (1 Corinthians 15:47). But after the one who had been formed from the earth went back into the earth, the one who became the second man ascended into the heavens. And it is said that there is a first Adam and a last Adam (1 Corinthians 15:45). Just as it is acknowledged that the second comes from the first as far as the flesh is concerned, which is why Christ is both man and Son of Man, so it is also testified that the second is the Savior of the first, for whose sake he even came down from heaven. And since the Word came down from heaven and, having become man, ascended into the heavens, for this reason the second Adam is also said to be from heaven (1 Corinthians 15:47).
notes: Homo perfectus kept as the doctrinal term “perfect man” (complete humanity).
“Like one of the prophets” keeps tanquam unum ex prophetis (unum agrees with hominem) and its ambiguity: the rejected view treats the man Christ took up as one more prophet.
Edition margin at a Christo has al. a Domino, and at a Domino (interpretatio) al. a Christo; the text readings are kept, and the sense does not change.
At cursum temporum complevit the margin gives a variant (et numeratione temporum suscept…, last word blurred); text reading kept; “the appointed” dropped in review as not in the Latin.
Born in Bethlehem and brought up in Nazareth summarise Luke 2:4–7, 39–40 and are left uncited as narrative summary.
The Word coming down from heaven and ascending may echo John 3:13; left uncited as uncertain.
Primus Adam … novissimus Adam is reported speech (dicitur), rendered “it is said”.
